definition: Small language models (SLM) or compact language models are artificial intelligence language models designed for human natural language processing including language and text generation.
details: Small language models typically have less than forty billion parameters. This make them feasible to train or host entirely on consumer electronics such as personal computers, laptops, or smart devices. In contrast, a large language model typically contains hundreds of billions of training parameters, with some models exceeding a trillion parameters. This enables the model to encode vast amounts of information, improving the generalizability and accuracy of its outputs. However, training and hosting such models demands enormous computational resources, rendering it infeasible for an individual to do so using a single computer and graphics processing unit. Most contemporary small language models use the same architecture as a large language model, but with a smaller parameter count and sometimes lower arithmetic precision. Similar to LLMs, SLMs are optimized via knowledge distillation, pruning, and quantization.

explainer.lead: Small language models are language models built for natural language processing and text generation with far fewer parameters than large models. Their size makes them feasible to train or host entirely on consumer electronics such as personal computers, laptops or smart devices.

tiers.eli5: It's a language model small enough to live on your own laptop instead of needing a giant data centre.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy SLMs on-device and optimize them with knowledge distillation, pruning and quantization. The pitfall is that the smaller parameter count limits how much information the model encodes, which can reduce generalizability and accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: Small language models typically have fewer than forty billion parameters, often share the architecture of large language models at lower parameter count and sometimes lower arithmetic precision, and are optimized via distillation, pruning and quantization; large models typically contain hundreds of billions of parameters, some exceeding a trillion.

explainer.example: A model with a few billion parameters from a family such as Gemma, which includes models under ten billion parameters, can run locally on a laptop.
